summary: Nancy S. Steinhardt is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She became a professor of East Asian art at the University of Pennsylvania and curator of Chinese art at the Penn Museum circa 1982.

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and was a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies in 2011.
Nandini Gooptu is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 2026, she is attested as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at both the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

Nanigopal Majumdar (1897–1938) was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He became a Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1931 and served as Superintendent of the Arch&aelogic&al Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).
Nantu Shaw is an Indologist and philosopher who studied as a Visiting Scholar at Stony Brook University under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

Nao Kasamatsu is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Kasamatsu served as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Sendai College (attested 2015) and as a part-time lecturer at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985). He served as an assistant and lecturer at Tohoku University (~1985–1993) before becoming a professor at Koyasan University (~1993–2021).
Naoki Kano (1868–1947) was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893). He held a post at Kyoto University beginning in 1906.
Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar attested in 2004 as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University, an institution he founded.
Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Tohoku University by 2002 under Toshifumi Goto. At Tohoku University, she was an expert researcher in 2012 and a professor in 2026.

Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist, Indological, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at Oxford under supervisors Christopher Minkowski and David N. Gellner, and later became a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff and a professor at the University of Edinburgh.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford under Takakusu, Macdonell, Geldner, and Lévi. He became Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960) and directed Toyo Bunko (1974).
Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and held a post at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Ceylon University College, and under Pelene Siri Vajiragnana. He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya from circa 1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani (1924–2013) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD as a research fellow at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held posts at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1970, 1990, and 1999.

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo and Calcutta (PhD 1985). He held appointments at CEACS, Toyo Bunko, Kobe University, and served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1996–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1974 and 1988.
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University in 2001 and became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–1975) under Stephan Beyer, also studying with Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
